advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Choose a distinct default host port for AUTOLANDER_PORT (e.g. 8090) so it does not collide with Gerrit's fixed 127.0.0.1:8080 publish.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:38: `- "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"` (gerrit)
docker-compose.yml:130: `- "127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080"` (autolander)
fetch-secrets.sh:114: `echo "AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080"`
Dockerfile.autolander:51: `ENV AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080`
advisory.finding: The autolander container publishes its status endpoint on host loopback 127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080, and fetch-secrets.sh writes AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080 — the SAME host address:port the Gerrit container already binds (127.0.0.1:8080:8080). Two services cannot bind the same host loopback port; the autolander (or gerrit) container will fail to start with a port-allocation error.
scenarios: compose up / autodeploy of the autolander service on the box where gerrit already binds 127.0.0.1:8080
advisory.suggested_fix: Set AUTOLANDER_PORT default to a free port (e.g. 8090) in fetch-secrets.sh, Dockerfile.autolander, and the nginx template; the container port can stay 8080 since it is namespaced per-container.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Point AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL at the autolander's real published port (matching the corrected AUTOLANDER_PORT), not Gerrit's 8080.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:51: `AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL="${AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL:-http://localhost:8080/}"  # auto-lander status endpoint (NOT Gerrit)`
docker-compose.yml:38: gerrit binds `127.0.0.1:8080:8080`
autodeploy.sh:207-ish: `while ... curl -fsS -m 3 "$AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL" ... done`
advisory.finding: AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL defaults to http://localhost:8080/, which is Gerrit's published loopback port, not the autolander's. Given the port collision above, the post-deploy health check either probes Gerrit (falsely reporting the autolander healthy) or never reaches the autolander at all.
scenarios: autodeploy rebuilds the autolander and probes 8080 — hits Gerrit, giving a green health check regardless of autolander state
advisory.suggested_fix: Set AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL to http://localhost:${AUTOLANDER_PORT}/ once AUTOLANDER_PORT is de-conflicted from Gerrit's 8080.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` references (commit msg, setup-project.sh text, smoke-check messages) with project.config's assertion that only the `rebase` right exists.
evidence: project.config:67-69: `On Gerrit 3.14.1 this is authorized by the per-ref `rebase` access right alone ... there is no separate `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` ref permission; that form is silently ignored`
project.config:75-76: only `rebase = group Contributors` / `rebase = group Administrators` are added
smoke-check-autolander.sh header: `requires the bot identity ... to hold BOTH the per-ref `rebase` AND `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` access rights`
smoke-check-autolander.sh 403 branch: `bot lacks rebase / rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader on refs/heads/*`
setup-project.sh:148: commit message `rebase/rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant`
ticket 3c55 AC S5b: `the `All-Projects` `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` capability + submit ACL via `setup-all-projects.sh``
ticket file_impact for setup-project.sh: `All-Projects [capability] rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader + submit on refs/heads/*`
diff adds `rebase` to project.config [access "refs/heads/*"], not an All-Projects capability
setup-all-projects.sh does not appear in the 12 changed files
advisory.finding: The changeset is internally contradictory about `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader`: the commit message, setup-project.sh commit text, and smoke-check-autolander.sh all assert the bot needs BOTH a `rebase` AND a `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` access right, but project.config's own comment states there is no separate `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` ref permission (it is 'silently ignored') and grants only `rebase`. The smoke check's 403 failure message and step-5 rationale reference a grant that the config says does not exist.
merged_from: The implementation diverges from the story's Acceptance Criteria: rebar-ticket S5b specifies an All-Projects `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` CAPABILITY plus submit ACL provisioned via setup-all-projects.sh, but the diff instead adds a per-ref `rebase` ACCESS RIGHT in project.config and does not touch setup-all-projects.sh at all (it is not in the changeset).
scenarios: operator debugging a smoke-check 403 chases a nonexistent rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant that the config author says is ignored
advisory.suggested_fix: If only `rebase` is authoritative, remove `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` mentions from the smoke-check messages and commit messages; otherwise add the grant to project.config.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the rebase-on-behalf ACL contradiction: confirm against Gerrit 3.14.1 whether on_behalf_of_uploader needs `rebase` alone or also `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader`, and reconcile project.config vs smoke-check-autolander.sh.
evidence: project.config:67-69: 'On Gerrit 3.14.1 this is authorized by the per-ref `rebase` access right alone (verified against GET /projects/rebar/access — there is no separate `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` ref permission; that form is silently ignored).'
smoke-check-autolander.sh:8-10: 'That REST option requires the bot identity (RebarBotNava, a member of `Contributors`) to hold BOTH the per-ref `rebase` AND `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` access rights'

Only `rebase = group Contributors` / `rebase = group Administrators` are actually added (project.config:75-76); no `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` line is present, so the two docs disagree on whether the granted ACL is sufficient or over-broad.
advisory.finding: Contradictory authorization claims for rebase-on-behalf-of-uploader within the same changeset: smoke-check-autolander.sh states the bot must hold BOTH `rebase` AND `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader`, while project.config asserts `rebase` alone authorizes on_behalf_of_uploader and `rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader` is silently ignored. If project.config is correct, granting `rebase` confers uploader-impersonation; if smoke-check is correct, the grant is incomplete and rebase-on-behalf will 403.
scenarios: Deploy: setup-project.sh pushes the config; if smoke-check's claim holds, the bot cannot rebase-on-behalf and landing silently fails (fail-closed but breaks the story).
If project.config's claim holds, `rebase` alone is enough to create patchsets attributed to another user — a stronger capability than intended.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the rebase / rebase-on-behalf grant to the landing-bot identity (a dedicated group) rather than the whole operator-extensible Contributors group.
evidence: project.config:75: 'rebase = group Contributors'
project.config:71: 'Granted to Contributors (RebarBotNava, the landing bot, is a member) + Administrators'
setup-project.sh:91-92: 'CONTRIBUTOR_MEMBERS="${CONTRIBUTOR_MEMBERS:-RebarBotNava}" ... Set CONTRIBUTOR_MEMBERS to override the default list' — the group is not bot-only.
ticket S5b AC scoped this to the bot identity's landing capability, not a group-wide impersonation grant.
advisory.finding: The `rebase` access right (which enables on_behalf_of_uploader — producing patchsets attributed to a different, original uploader) is granted to the entire `Contributors` group, not only the landing bot. Contributors membership is operator-extensible (setup-project.sh: Administrators + CONTRIBUTOR_MEMBERS), so any current/future Contributor gains an uploader-impersonation capability beyond the single-bot scope the story describes.
scenarios: A non-bot Contributor uses POST /changes/{id}/rebase with on_behalf_of_uploader=true to create a patchset attributed to another engineer.
Operator adds human contributors to CONTRIBUTORS for the submit gate and unintentionally also confers rebase-on-behalf impersonation.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the autoheal image to a specific version + sha256 digest (and consider a read-only/socket-proxy mount) since it holds RW /var/run/docker.sock.
evidence: docker-compose.yml: 'image: willfarrell/autoheal' — no tag/digest pin (resolves to mutable :latest).
docker-compose.yml: '- /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock' with comment 'Needs the Docker socket (read-write) to inspect health + issue container restarts.'
Other services (gerrit, review-bot, autolander) use build.context locally; autoheal is the sole third-party pulled image and carries the most privileged mount.
advisory.finding: The autoheal sidecar mounts the Docker socket read-write while using an unpinned mutable image tag (`willfarrell/autoheal`, no version or digest). A compromised or re-pushed upstream `:latest` would execute with full read-write Docker control on the host (root-equivalent), and it is the only externally-pulled image in this compose stack (all others build locally).
scenarios: Upstream account/tag compromise or a malicious re-push of willfarrell/autoheal:latest is pulled on the next deploy and gains host Docker control via the RW socket.
No digest pin means the image cannot be reproducibly audited across deploys.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pin the image, e.g. `image: willfarrell/autoheal:1.2.0@sha256:<digest>`, and consider fronting the socket with a read-scoped docker-socket-proxy limited to container inspect/restart.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the autolander a distinct host port (AUTOLANDER_PORT != 8080) since Gerrit already publishes 127.0.0.1:8080.
evidence: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:38 gerrit: `- "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml (autolander) `- "127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080"`
infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh: `echo "AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080"`
infra/compose/Dockerfile.autolander: `ENV AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080`
advisory.finding: The autolander service binds the same host loopback port as Gerrit: docker-compose maps gerrit to `127.0.0.1:8080:8080` and autolander to `127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT:-8080}:8080`, and fetch-secrets.sh writes AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080, so both containers try to publish 127.0.0.1:8080 — a hard bind conflict that prevents the stack from starting.
scenarios: compose-up / autodeploy brings up both gerrit and autolander on the same box
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the default AUTOLANDER_PORT (Dockerfile ENV + fetch-secrets.sh + docs) to a free host port such as 8090, keeping the container port at 8080.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure AUTOLANDER_PORT resolves to a port distinct from Gerrit's 8080 so the nginx /autolander/status route reaches the lander.
evidence: infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:69 `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT}/;`
infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:86 `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;` (Gerrit)
infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh sets AUTOLANDER_PORT=8080
advisory.finding: With AUTOLANDER_PORT defaulting to 8080, the nginx `/autolander/status` route proxies to `127.0.0.1:${AUTOLANDER_PORT}` = 127.0.0.1:8080, which is Gerrit's published port (nginx proxies Gerrit at a hardcoded 127.0.0.1:8080), so the status route would reach Gerrit rather than the auto-lander.
scenarios: Operator hits /autolander/status once nginx is reloaded with the templated port

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Point AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL at the autolander's actual host port, not Gerrit's 8080.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:51 `AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL="${AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL:-http://localhost:8080/}"  # auto-lander status endpoint (NOT Gerrit)`
infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:50 review-bot `HEALTH_URL=...:8000/health`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:38 Gerrit publishes 127.0.0.1:8080
advisory.finding: autodeploy's AUTOLANDER_HEALTH_URL defaults to `http://localhost:8080/`, which is Gerrit's port (HEALTH_URL for review-bot correctly points at 8000). The post-deploy health check and rollback for the autolander would probe Gerrit, so an unhealthy autolander could pass (or Gerrit could mask the lander's state).
scenarios: autodeploy rebuilds the autolander and runs the status-endpoint health gate

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the autoheal image to a specific tag or digest (e.g. willfarrell/autoheal:1.2.0 / @sha256:...).
evidence: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml `image: willfarrell/autoheal` (no tag)
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:28 gerrit pinned to `gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1`
infra/compose/docker-compose.yml `- /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock`
comment: `Needs the Docker socket (read-write) to inspect health + issue container restarts.`
advisory.finding: The autoheal sidecar image is unpinned (`image: willfarrell/autoheal` with no tag/digest), resolving to :latest, unlike every other image in the stack (gerritcodereview/gerrit:3.14.1, python:3.12-slim). This introduces version drift — an upstream :latest change alters restart behavior on any re-pull.
merged_from: The autoheal sidecar mounts the Docker socket read-write (`/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock`), granting the container full Docker daemon control (root-equivalent on the host). This is a large blast radius for a container whose stated need is only to inspect health and restart one labelled container.
scenarios: Host re-pulls the autoheal image after an upstream release
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `image: willfarrell/autoheal` with a pinned tag or digest.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align setup-project.sh's commit message with the actual project.config change (only the `rebase` access right is granted).
evidence: infra/gerrit/setup-project.sh commit msg: `+ rebase/rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant (auto-lander FFO rebase, S5b)`
infra/gerrit/project.config:75-76 only `rebase = group Contributors` / `rebase = group Administrators`
infra/gerrit/project.config:68-69 comment: `there is no separate rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader ref permission; that form is silently ignored`
advisory.finding: setup-project.sh's commit message claims a 'rebase/rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader grant' was added, but project.config only adds the boolean `rebase` access right (the config comment itself states rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader is not a real ref permission and is 'silently ignored'). The committed ACL and its description diverge.
scenarios: Operator reads git log of refs/meta/config to audit the granted ACLs
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop 'rebaseOnBehalfOfUploader' from the setup-project.sh commit message, referencing only the `rebase` grant.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make smoke-check-autolander.sh step-5 fail (not WARN-then-PASS) when the rebased patch set uploader cannot be read, so an unverified on_behalf_of_uploader outcome never reports PASS.
evidence: header claims step 5 'proves on_behalf_of_uploader took effect, not a plain bot rebase' (smoke-check-autolander.sh:24-25)
`if [ -z "${uploader_username}" ]; then echo "...WARN — could not read the rebased patch set uploader; skipping the uploader-preservation assertion..."` (smoke-check-autolander.sh:121-122)
the uploader parse swallows errors: `python3 -c '...' 2>/dev/null || true` (smoke-check-autolander.sh:119) so any JSON-shape drift or missing username/email yields empty string -> WARN path
final line unconditionally prints `smoke-check-autolander: PASS — auto-lander rebase-on-behalf grant verified.` (smoke-check-autolander.sh:129) even after the WARN skip
advisory.finding: smoke-check-autolander.sh step-5 asserts too little: the uploader-preservation check (the script's raison d'être — proving on_behalf_of_uploader took effect vs a plain bot rebase) is swallowed on an empty/unparseable uploader (WARN branch) yet the script still prints 'PASS — grant verified', so the strongest half of the contract can silently no-op while self-reporting success.
scenarios: Gerrit detail JSON omits username (DETAILED_ACCOUNTS returns only account_id/name), so uploader_username is empty; a plain bot rebase (on-behalf grant NOT effective) then passes the smoke check as PASS
future Gerrit response-shape change breaks the python parse; step 5 silently degrades to a no-op
advisory.suggested_fix: In the `[ -z "${uploader_username}" ]` branch call `fail` (or exit SKIP before the final PASS line) rather than WARN-and-continue, so an unreadable uploader does not culminate in a PASS verdict; also drop the `2>/dev/null` on the python parse so a parse error is visible.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a config-check.sh invariant (mirroring §1b) asserting the auto-lander `rebase` grant stays a per-ref access right on refs/heads/* and does not co-occur with a submit grant or an All-Projects capability.
evidence: new grant added: `rebase = group Contributors` / `rebase = group Administrators` (project.config:75-76)
commit + comment emphasize it is a security-scoped grant: 'NOT an All-Projects global capability and does NOT grant submit' (project.config:71-73)

existing precedent that new security-sensitive project.config grants get a CI-gate invariant: config-check.sh §1b 'Autosubmit label security invariants' asserts non-gating/non-sticky + vote-ACL scope (config-check.sh:38-58)
config-check.sh was NOT extended in this diff (not in changed-files list); ABSENCE: no test references `rebase` grant scope (search 'rebaseOnBehalf' in tests/ -> no matches)
advisory.finding: No CI-gate invariant guards the new security-sensitive `rebase`/rebase-on-behalf per-ref grant, despite the project's established precedent of asserting such invariants at the config-check gate (§1b guards the Autosubmit label). The commit repeatedly asserts the grant is NOT submit and NOT a global capability, but nothing tests that it stays scoped, so drift into a `[capability]` block or an added `submit` grant on refs/heads/* would not be caught.
scenarios: a later edit adds `submit = group Contributors` or promotes the grant to an All-Projects [capability]; config-check passes (still valid git-config) and the scope-widening reaches main unnoticed
